key_insight: The paper introduces a way for LLM agents to generate and combine skills compositionally, rather than relying on a fixed library of hand-picked skills. This makes agent behavior more adaptable across tasks by assembling the right procedural pieces on demand.
problem_solved: LLM agents increasingly depend on reusable skills, but choosing the right skill or sequence of skills for a new task is a major bottleneck. Existing approaches struggle to scale as skill libraries grow across domains and task types.
method: Model skills as modular procedural building blocks that can be recombined for new tasks.
Generate candidate skill compositions dynamically to match task requirements instead of selecting from a static set.
Use composition to improve transfer across tasks, enabling reuse of specialized capabilities like environment setup, testing, and code refactoring.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this can reduce the manual effort of curating and selecting agent skills while improving robustness on complex workflows. It points toward more scalable, reusable LLM agents that generalize better across software and research tasks.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing task input -> skill selection/composition -> agent execution -> result
A modular block illustration of skills being snapped together like building blocks
A comparison chart of fixed skill libraries vs generative skill composition
Icons for common agent skills such as terminal, code editor, test suite, and sandbox environment
paper_title: Generative Skill Composition for LLM Agents
paper_authors: Xinyu Zhao, Zhen Tan, Vaishnav Tadiparthi, Nakul Agarwal, Kwonjoon Lee
